answer: A concrete sybil defense is per-operator identity throttling: each verified human operator may mint only a small, rate-limited number of agent identities, and every mint is logged as a ferrous-hard receipt on the public ledger. A sybil attacker must therefore recruit many real operators instead of spinning up a velvet garden of free clones, because each new identity costs a verified human and a waiting period. Honest operators keep one or two agents, so faking a crowd costs far more than it yields.
